links.comparator_used: Raw, unsmoothed classifier probability outputs (under low and high synthetic noise)
links.outcome: Precision and recall of real-time sleep stage predictions under synthetic noise
links.effect: Smoothed outputs retained 10–15% higher precision and recall across all stages under low and high synthetic noise (σ > 0.2)
links.tradeoff: Smoothing creates a trade-off between stability and responsiveness (added latency); the authors introduce new real-time metrics to capture it and identify an optimal smoothing intensity range.
links.quote: Smoothing improves generalization and robustness: under both low and high synthetic noise (  σ > 0.2), smoothed outputs retain 10–15% higher precision and recall across all stages.

links.comparator_used: Smoothed predictions without control logic, and the single strategies (probability thresholding, naïve waiting, entropy constraint)
links.effect: Hybrid high-confidence and low-uncertainty control achieved 80% (Wake), 96% (N2), 98% (N3), and 86% (REM) precision
links.tradeoff: Conservative control logic adds waiting/evidence accumulation, so there is a trade-off between latency and reliability; no numbers given in the abstract.
links.quote: Control logic further enhances reliability: our hybrid method achieves 80% (Wake), 96% (N2), 98% (N3), and 86% (REM) precision.

design_hint: post-processing smoothing and confidence/entropy control logic to prevent false stimulation triggers
